batchName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE)

questions.question: Who was keeping Antony's will before Octavian seized it?
questions.explanation: The will was held by the Vestal Virgins, priestesses of Rome's sacred hearth. A defector tipped off Octavian, who seized and read it.
questions.sourceQuote: Then a defector told Octavian about Antony's will, kept by the Vestal Virgins (*virgines Vestales*), the priestesses of Rome's sacred hearth.

questions.question: What did Caesar's assassins call themselves?
questions.explanation: The killers styled themselves liberators (liberatores), freeing Rome from a dictator. At first they were even pardoned.
questions.sourceQuote: His killers called themselves the liberators (*liberatores*).

questions.question: Where did Antony summon Cleopatra to meet him after Philippi?
questions.explanation: Antony summoned the Greek-speaking queen of Egypt to Cilicia, on the southern coast of modern Turkey, and they soon began an affair.
questions.sourceQuote: He summoned Cleopatra, the Greek-speaking queen of Egypt, to meet him in Cilicia, on the southern coast of modern Turkey.

questions.question: Who was the third man who joined Antony and Octavian to form the triumvirate?
questions.explanation: Lepidus, a Caesarian general commanding in the west, hosted the meeting where the three men struck their deal in northern Italy.
questions.sourceQuote: Urged on by their soldiers, the two met in northern Italy under the protection of Lepidus, a Caesarian general commanding in the west.

questions.question: In what year was Julius Caesar assassinated on the Ides of March?
questions.explanation: Caesar was stabbed to death by a band of senators on 15 March 44 BC. Afterwards an uneasy compromise briefly held in Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: On 15 March 44 BC, Julius Caesar, the dictator who had made himself master of Rome, was stabbed to death by a band of senators.

questions.question: Which famous virtue of Julius Caesar did the triumvirs declare had been a mistake?
questions.explanation: The triumvirs announced that Caesar's mercy had been a mistake, and attached a list of men to be killed.
questions.sourceQuote: They issued a declaration that Caesar's famous mercy (*clementia*) had been a mistake, and attached a list of men to be killed.

questions.question: Near which headland in western Greece was Antony camped before his decisive sea battle in 31 BC?
questions.explanation: Antony camped at Actium, a headland at the mouth of a bay on the Ionian coast. Octavian's admiral then cut his supply lines.
questions.sourceQuote: Antony gathered a huge force in western Greece, camping at Actium, a headland at the mouth of a bay on the Ionian coast.

questions.question: What happened to a man named on a proscription list?
options: He lost his right to vote in the assemblies
He was barred from the Senate for five years
He could be killed on sight and his property seized
He was exiled to an island but kept his estates
questions.explanation: Anyone proscribed could be murdered on sight, and his property was seized and sold. Bounty hunters and informers were paid cash for each death.
questions.sourceQuote: This was a proscription (*proscriptio*): anyone named could be murdered on sight, and his property was seized and sold.

questions.question: How was Octavian related to Julius Caesar?
options: He was his great-nephew and adopted heir
He was his nephew by marriage
questions.explanation: Octavian was Caesar's great-nephew and adopted heir. He used that connection to lure Caesar's veterans away from Antony.
questions.sourceQuote: Octavian, Caesar's great-nephew and adopted heir, lured Caesar's veterans away from Antony and raised a private army.

questions.question: Who was hailed "King of Kings" at the Donations of Alexandria?
questions.explanation: Cleopatra's son by Julius Caesar was hailed King of Kings, a direct challenge to Octavian's claim to be Caesar's only heir.
questions.sourceQuote: Her son by Julius Caesar was hailed "King of Kings", a direct challenge to Octavian's claim to be Caesar's only heir.
